key_insight: The paper shows how to spend a limited annotation budget optimally in off-policy evaluation by choosing which sequential rewards to label, reducing estimator variance while preserving trustworthy policy-value estimates.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical evaluation of AI or decision-making systems when labels are expensive or noisy, such as expert review of safety cases, clinical notes, or human preference data.
method: Uses doubly robust off-policy evaluation with missing rewards.
Derives variance-optimal annotation probabilities for sequential forward-monotone annotation.
Provides a feasible batch-adaptive implementation for real annotation workflows.
evidence_signal: In simulations and on two real datasets, the method reduced RMSE by 34–65% on the homelessness casenote task and 55–62% on LMArena across evaluated budgets.
watch_item: The approach depends on a workable annotation protocol and cost model, so performance may degrade if annotation availability, bias, or sequential constraints differ from the assumed setting.
paper_title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
